comparisons.peer_topic: Inventory write-down impact on gross margin
comparisons.peer_summary: If assumptions regarding future demand or market conditions become less favorable, additional inventory write-downs may be required, negatively impacting gross margin; conversely, selling previously written-down inventory above its written-down value may result in a net benefit to gross margin.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD explicitly discuss the mechanics of inventory provisions and their specific impact on gross margin, covering both the negative impact of new write-downs and the positive benefit from selling previously reserved inventory. NVDA quantifies this with $2.2 billion in provisions and a $540 million release impacting gross margin by -2.7% and +0.6% respectively (net unfavorable). AMD discloses the same dynamic conceptually, stating that additional write-downs result in a negative impact to gross margin, while selling written-down inventory below its realized selling price results in a net benefit, though AMD does not provide the specific 2024 dollar amounts or percentage impacts in this specific snippet.

sentences.text: Provisions for inventory and excess inventory purchase obligations totaled $2.2 billion for both fiscal years 2024 and 2023.

Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The net effect on our gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% and 7.5% in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

If in any period we anticipate a change in assumptions such as future demand or market conditions to be less favorable than our previous estimates, additional inventory write-downs may be required and would be reflected in cost of sales, resulting in a negative impact to our gross margin in that period.

If in any period we are able to sell inventories that had been written down to a level below the ultimate realized selling price in a previous period, related revenue would be recorded with a lower or no offsetting charge to cost of sales resulting in a net benefit to our gross margin in that period.

peer_results.rationale: The peer candidate avgo_2024_7_D073 discusses employee withholding taxes, which is unrelated to inventory provisions. The peer candidate avgo_2024_7_D049 discusses gross margin results but attributes changes to VMware and amortization, without specific detail on inventory write-down provisions or releases comparable to the target.

comparisons.peer_summary: The 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by favorable movements including lower period charges from sell-through of previously reserved inventory, lower non-accelerator reserves, lower excess capacity charges, and benefits from CHIPS Act government incentives.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and INTC disclose specific favorable movements in gross margin driven by the 'sell-through of previously reserved inventory.' NVDA reports a $540 million provision release from such sales in 2024, contributing to a net unfavorable gross margin impact of 2.7%. Similarly, INTC identifies 'lower period charges driven by the sell-through of previously reserved inventory' as a key favorable movement that partially offset unfavorable impacts in 2024. Both companies treat the release of reserves via inventory sales as a distinct driver of gross margin performance, contrasting with the initial provision charges.

sentences.text: Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The net effect on our gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% and 7.5% in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

These 2024 unfavorable gross margin impacts were partially offset by certain favorable gross margin movements in 2024, including lower period charges driven by the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower non-accelerator reserves taken, lower period charges related to excess capacity charges, and a benefit recognized for government incentives received under the CHIPS Act.

comparisons.peer_topic: NEX Cost of Sales Changes and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Network and Edge cost of sales decreased $638 million from 2023, primarily due to lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower reserves taken in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison focuses on the specific segment impact of inventory reserve changes. Both NVDA and INTC highlight 'lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory' as a positive factor for cost of sales/gross margin. NVDA reports a $540 million release from this activity for the consolidated company. INTC specifically attributes a $638 million decrease in NEX (Network and Edge) cost of sales to this same factor, along with lower reserves taken. Both disclosures link the reduction in charges directly to the realization/sale of previously reserved inventory.

sentences.text: Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
▪NEX cost of sales decreased $638 million from 2023, primarily driven by lower period charges from the sell-through of previously reserved inventory and lower reserves taken in 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and MU disclose the specific benefit to gross margin derived from selling inventories that had been previously written down. NVDA quantifies this as a $540 million provision release in 2024. MU explicitly attributes part of its 2024 margin improvement to 'lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023.' While the timing differs (NVDA references releases in the current fiscal year vs prior, while MU references 2024 sales of 2023 writedowns), both identify the same specific financial phenomenon: the margin accretion resulting from selling inventory held at lower, reserved values.

sentences.text: Sales of previously reserved inventory or settlements of excess inventory purchase obligations resulted in a provision release of $540 million and $137 million for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The net effect on our gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% and 7.5% in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).

peer_results.rationale: The peer candidates qcom_2024_7_D011 and qcom_2024_7_D024 only state that gross margin was flat; they do not provide substantive detail on inventory provisions, write-downs, or reserve releases that would allow for a comparable analysis of the specific topic.
